faq.a: A corporate bond is a debt instrument issued by a company to raise capital. When you buy a corporate bond, you are essentially lending money to the company, which promises to pay you regular interest (coupon payments) and return your principal amount on a specified maturity date.

faq.q: How are corporate bonds different from fixed deposits?
faq.a: While both are fixed-income instruments, corporate bonds carry credit risk (the risk of the company defaulting), unlike bank fixed deposits which are generally considered very safe, especially if covered by deposit insurance. Corporate bonds can offer higher interest rates than FDs but also come with higher risk and can be traded in the secondary market, leading to price fluctuations.

faq.q: What is credit rating in bonds?
faq.a: A credit rating is an assessment of a bond issuer's ability to meet its financial obligations. Agencies like CRISIL, ICRA, and CARE assign ratings (e.g., AAA, AA, BBB) to bonds, indicating their creditworthiness. A higher rating generally signifies lower risk of default.

faq.q: Will these changes make bonds risk-free?
faq.a: No, the proposed changes will not make corporate bonds risk-free. While the distributor network aims to simplify access and tighter ad rules will enhance transparency, corporate bonds will always carry inherent risks, primarily credit risk and interest rate risk. Investors must still understand and assess these risks.

faq.q: How can I find a bond distributor once the system is in place?
faq.a: Once SEBI finalises and implements the framework, there will likely be an official registry or a list of certified bond distributors available on the SEBI website or through stock exchanges, similar to how mutual fund distributors are listed.

faq.q: Are NRIs eligible to invest in these bonds?
faq.a: Generally, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) are permitted to invest in Indian corporate bonds, often through designated NRO or NRE accounts. However, specific regulations and eligibility criteria might vary based on the type of bond and prevailing RBI/SEBI guidelines. It's advisable for NRIs to check the latest regulations or consult a financial advisor.
